property_summary: For any caller, setOwner should update owner only if the caller is the admin; the mutant allows any caller to set owner, so after a non-admin call owner changes incorrectly.
For any call to setOwner from an address that is not the admin, the owner must remain unchanged; the mutant breaks this by allowing a non-admin to change the owner.
Only the admin can successfully change the owner; the buggy version allows any caller to change it.
After setOwner is called by the admin with any address argument, the owner state variable must be updated to that argument; the buggy version leaves owner unchanged.

After a successful setOwner call by the admin, the owner state variable must equal the argument _owner; the mutant sets it to msg.sender instead, violating this rule when msg.sender differs from _owner.
After any call to setOwner, the owner state variable must equal the argument passed; the mutant sets it to address(0) regardless of the argument, breaking the rule for any non-zero address.
For any call to setOwner that does not revert, the return value must be true; the buggy mutant returns false even when the operation succeeds.
For any admin call to setOwner, the return value must be true; the buggy version returns false thus violating the invariant.
For any admin caller, `setOwner` must return `true`; the buggy version omits the return statement causing it to implicitly return `false`.
After any call to setOwner, the owner should only change if the caller was the original admin; the mutant allows any caller to change it.
